Fixed 2026-07-30: clients.pin/team_members.pin encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM via existing secret-crypto.ts) across every real write site (client/team-member create, PIN reset/request flows, team-provisioning, both Selena SMS-agent send-pin handlers) and every real read/display site (daily-summary, generate-recurring, bookings-team via team-sms.ts, broadcast-guidelines, notify.ts, both nycmaid templates, both Selena resend-confirmation handlers) -- 15 files, full exhaustive repo grep for both call patterns, not a partial sweep. Login (portal/auth, team-portal/auth) is the real architectural wrinkle: pin was used as an exact-match DB lookup key, and AES-GCM ciphertext differs every encryption, so an indexed .eq() lookup cannot find an encrypted row. Fixed with a two-tier lookup (src/lib/pin-lookup.ts): fast .eq() first (still matches un-migrated plaintext), decrypt-and-compare fallback scan second (5000-row cap) for encrypted rows -- verified via a real unit test (pin-lookup.test.ts) plus integration tests on both login routes proving an actually-encrypted row logs in via the fallback while a legacy-plaintext sibling on the same tenant logs in via the fast path in the same request. Full suite (892 files/5006 tests) passes, typecheck and lint clean. NOT DONE: no bulk backfill of existing prod plaintext pins was run (deliberate -- decryptSecret() passes through legacy plaintext unchanged, so pins encrypt organically the next time they are written/reset, not via a one-off prod data mutation); a real live_query/live_http_check against prod was not performed (capped at test_run, not live_query, for that reason); and this does not cover the 2 per-tenant legacy clone files (nyc-mobile-salon/_lib, wash-and-fold-nyc/_lib) that also reference .pin, flagged as a known, disclosed gap, not silently skipped.

Reviewed 2026-07-31 -- this checkpoint's prior 'not_scored' entry stated no Supabase Management API read endpoint exists for backup/PITR state. That was wrong (or the API changed): GET /v1/projects/{ref}/database/backups DOES return it, no dashboard access needed. The real gap: Point-In-Time Recovery is OFF. With PITR disabled, a restore can only land on one of these daily snapshots (up to ~24h of data loss on the worst possible incident timing); with it enabled, restore could target any specific moment. For a live-revenue platform this is a real, live risk, not a hypothetical -- and now a known, specific one instead of an unknown. Enabling PITR is a Supabase plan/add-on decision (cost + Jeff sign-off), not something this session can flip via API. live_query evidence, cap 100 -- scored on the actual state found (reliable daily backups = a real baseline; PITR off = a real, named gap), not at ceiling.

Fixed 2026-07-31 (worker w3, commit 49ce1856d): a real reliability risk found during re-check -- none of translateToEnEs()'s 7 real callers (every Loop Connect send route) set an explicit Next.js maxDuration, so they run under Vercel's own (short) platform-level function timeout, while the Anthropic SDK's own default per-request timeout is 10 minutes (confirmed via direct read of the installed node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/client.js: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 600000). The existing fail-open try/catch only protects against the awaited call throwing or returning something unparseable -- NOT against the call simply being slow, in which case a platform-level timeout would kill the whole request (the message send itself, not just the translation) before that catch block ever runs, defeating the 'translation failure must never block a send' design goal. Fixed: messages.create() now passes { timeout: 8000 }, so a slow response fails fast into the existing fail-open path well within any realistic platform timeout. 2 new tests (9 total in connect-translate.test.ts, all pass): confirms the timeout option is actually threaded through to the real SDK call, and that a timeout-shaped rejection still resolves via fail-open. tsc --noEmit clean; full test suite green (903 files, 5059 tests, 3 expected-fail, 37 skipped, unaffected).
